extraction.name: PIQA
extraction.description: PIQA (Physical Interaction: Question Answering) is a benchmark dataset for physical commonsense reasoning in natural language. It consists of multiple-choice question answering examples with a goal and two possible solutions, where exactly one solution is correct, and is designed to evaluate models' knowledge of everyday physical interactions and affordances.
extraction.creator: Yonatan Bisk; Rowan Zellers; Ronan Le Bras; Jianfeng Gao; Yejin Choi
extraction.citeAs: Yonatan Bisk; Rowan Zellers; Ronan Le Bras; Jianfeng Gao; Yejin Choi. PIQA: Reasoning about Physical Commonsense in Natural Language. 2020.
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The dataset was collected by prompting annotators with links to instructables.com examples and asking them to construct goal-solution pairs inspired by those instructions, including a valid solution and an invalid permutation; examples were gathered in batches and low-agreement validation examples were removed.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionMissingData: During validation, examples with low agreement were removed from the data.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Links to instructables.com were used as prompts; the instructables website is described as a crowdsourced collection of instructions for tasks such as cooking, car repair, crafting, and manipulating objects using everyday materials.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Annotators were prompted with links to instructables.com, asked to glance at an instructable and construct two component tasks by articulating a physical goal and how to achieve it, then provide a permutation of their own solution that makes it invalid; qualification HITs were run beforehand, validation was done by other annotators for correctness, examples with low agreement were removed, and users with low agreement were de-qualified.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: During validation, examples with low agreement were removed from the data; human performance was calculated by a majority vote.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: reporting bias in language limits direct reporting of physical commonsense properties; unconstrained prompts led to reporting bias swamping the dataset, drawing annotators to prototypical solutions and kitchen/garage tools
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: examples with low agreement were removed, often including correct examples that required expert-level domain knowledge and thus should not fall under commonsense; some development-set model "mistakes" were actually correct but required a web search to verify; learning about the world from language alone is limiting
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: modeling physical commonsense knowledge is described as critical for day-to-day human life and for AI systems including robots that interact with the world and understand natural language; the authors aim to enable construction of language models useful beyond the NLP community
extraction.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: all data was collected in English
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: benchmarking progress in physical commonsense understanding; evaluating and studying physical commonsense understanding in natural language models; probing the inner workings of deep pretrained language models and determining the extent of their physical knowledge; providing a benchmark for progress toward language representations that capture physical knowledge useful for robotic-language applications
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: We asked annotators to provide semantic perturbations or alternative approaches which are otherwise syntactically and topically similar to ensure physical knowledge is targeted. In addition, we asked them to provide a permutation to their own solution which makes it invalid, often subtly. During validation, examples with low agreement were removed from the data. As noted previously, we use AFLite to remove stylistic artifacts and trivial examples from the data.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: During validation, examples with low agreement were removed from the data. As noted previously, we use AFLite to remove stylistic artifacts and trivial examples from the data. We compute edit distance over tokenized and lowercased strings with punctuation removed.
